decisions.claim: B is an interviewee who has had an interview
decisions.reason: A addresses B as 'you' throughout and instructs B to thank 'the interviewer' and 'say goodbye to the interviewer before you leave,' strongly presupposing B occupies the interviewee role. The interview is described as ongoing (turn 1: 'when the interview finally comes to an end'), so 'who has had an interview' is slightly imprecise but the core claim (B is an interviewee) is well-grounded.
decisions.counterexample: A could be giving generic advice to someone not currently in an interview, but the specific second-person instructions ('thank the interviewer again,' 'before you leave') make this unlikely.

decisions.claim: B has thanked the interviewer at least once prior to this moment
decisions.reason: 'Thank the interviewer again' contains the presupposition trigger 'again,' which logically requires that a prior thanking event occurred. This is a direct semantic presupposition.

decisions.claim: B is expected to receive a reply regarding the interview
decisions.reason: Turn 5 ('ask when you can receive a reply') and turn 9 ('the reply you get') both presuppose that B will receive a reply. 'The reply you get' uses a definite NP with a relative clause, entailing existence of a future reply for B.

decisions.claim: B is currently at the interview location with the interviewer present
decisions.reason: Turn 11 instructs B to 'say goodbye to the interviewer before you leave,' which presupposes B is currently at a location with the interviewer present and is about to leave. This is a necessary inference from the spatial deixis in the instruction.
decisions.counterexample: A could be giving hypothetical advice, but the use of 'again' and definite references to 'the interview' and 'the interviewer' indicate a real, current situation.

decisions.claim: B has already thanked the interviewer at least once during the interview
decisions.reason: c5 is bidirectionally equivalent to c2: both claim B thanked the interviewer at least once prior, both derive from the same presupposition trigger 'again' in turn 3. c2 is the more concise canonical statement.

decisions.claim: B is in the position of an interviewee/candidate who will receive a reply about interview results
decisions.reason: c6 restates c3 with slightly more verbose phrasing ('interviewee/candidate who will receive a reply about interview results'). Both are grounded in the same evidence (turns 5 and 9) and assert the same property: B is expected to receive a reply. c3 is the canonical form.

decisions.claim: B is expected to leave after the interview
decisions.reason: Turn 11 'before you leave' directly presupposes that B will leave the current location after the interview. This is a straightforward temporal presupposition from the subordinate clause.

decisions.claim: B was given an opportunity for the interview
decisions.reason: Turn 3 'thank the interviewer again for the opportunity of the interview' contains the definite NP 'the opportunity of the interview,' which presupposes that an opportunity was given to B. This is a clear existential presupposition.

decisions.claim: The interview has been ongoing and is nearing its end
decisions.reason: Turn 1 'When the interview finally comes to an end' presupposes the interview is currently ongoing (it hasn't ended yet) and that it is approaching its conclusion ('finally' implies duration and anticipation of the end). This is a direct temporal presupposition.

design: dual route, targeted rescue, globally grouped evidence adjudication
